text.description:
Text to render as a watermark. `${...}` references are resolved before rendering
text onto a PDF or image. Static text remains unchanged.

Use `${...}` markers with explicit namespaces, property access, and zero-based
list indices. These markers match document generation, but watermark expressions
are limited to value paths; full FreeMarker expressions and directives are not supported.

| Reference | Meaning | Example resolved value |
|---|---|---|
| `${attributes.CustomerName[0]}` | First value of `CustomerName` | `Acme` |
| `${attributes.Reviewer[1]}` | Second reviewer from `["Alice", "Bob"]` | `Bob` |
| `${attributes["Invoice.Number"][0]}` | Attribute whose key contains a dot | `INV-123` |
| `${attributes.Contract[0].customer.name}` | Property inside a JSON attribute | `Acme` |
| `${attributes.Contract[0].items[2].description}` | Third item inside that JSON object | `Third` |
| `${document.documentId}` | Standard document ID | `doc-123` |
| `${document.path}` | Standard document path | `invoice.pdf` |
| `${document.contentType}` | Standard document content type | `application/pdf` |
| `${document.insertedDate}` | Document creation date; example uses ISO 8601 UTC formatting | `2026-10-15T12:00:00Z` |
| `${metadata.Department}` | Custom document metadata | `Legal` |
| `${auth.username}` | Invocation username; defaults to `System` | `mike@example.com` |
| `${auth.claims["custom:department"]}` | Custom authentication claim | `Sales` |
| `${auth.claims.roles[0]}` | First role from `["reviewer", "editor"]` | `reviewer` |

Every document attribute is represented as a list, including a single-valued
attribute. In `attributes.Contract[0].items[2]`, `[0]` selects the attribute value
and `[2]` selects a JSON array element. Repeated scalar attribute values use
DynamoDB sort-key order, not original insertion order; JSON arrays retain their
own order.

Dots traverse properties. Single- or double-quoted bracket keys select exact
names containing dots, spaces, colons, or other punctuation. Within a quoted
key, a backslash escapes the next character. JSON attributes and claims retain
their native object, list, number, Boolean, and string types until a final value
is selected. Watermark text must select scalar values; whole objects and lists
are rejected.

The original placeholder is preserved for unknown
properties, null values, and out-of-range indices. Malformed paths are rejected.
Wildcards, slices, negative indices, and recursive descent are not supported.

Substitution runs once. Markers inside replacement values remain literal text.

The auth namespace uses authorization available to the watermark invocation.
The presigned-URL download flow does not forward the downloader's identity or
custom claims. Without supplied invocation authorization, auth.username resolves
to System and custom claim placeholders remain unchanged. The document.userId
field identifies the stored document's user and can differ from auth.username.

Variable_Watermark.description:
Given CustomerName values ["Acme"], document path "invoice.pdf", username
"mike@example.com", and custom:department claim "Sales" supplied to the watermark
invocation, the expected output is:

```text
Confidential — Acme
File: invoice.pdf
User: mike@example.com
Department: Sales
```

Indexed_Attribute_Watermark.summary: Indexed attribute values and literal keys
Indexed_Attribute_Watermark.description:
Given Reviewer values ["Alice", "Bob"] and the attribute key "Invoice.Number"
with values ["INV-123"], the expected rendered text is "Reviewed by Bob — INV-123".
`[1]` selects the second value; quoted brackets preserve the dot in the attribute key.

Auth_Claims_Watermark.description:
Given invocation claims {"custom:department": "Sales", "roles": ["reviewer", "editor"]},
the expected rendered text is "Sales — reviewer". These claims must be supplied to
the watermark invocation. The presigned-URL download flow does not forward them;
without those claims, the placeholders remain unchanged.
